Multiple crosses were carried out between plants with different flower colours (white, red, blue or purple) and the observations on the progeny phenotype are tabulated.
$\begin{array}{|l|l|} \\ \hline \text { cross } & \text { progeny phenotypes } \\ \hline \hline \text { White X White } & \text { All flowers are white } \\ \hline \text { Red X Red } & \begin{array}{l} \\ \text { All flowers are red or some are red and some are white (number } \\ \text { of red \gt \gt number of white) } \\ \end{array} \\ \hline \text { Blue X Blue } & \begin{array}{l} \\ \text { All flowers are blue or some are blue and some are white } \\ \text { (number of blue \gt \gt number of white) } \\ \end{array} \\ \hline \text { Purple X Purple } & \begin{array}{l} \\ \text { A mix of red, blue and purple flowers (number of purple flow- } \\ \text { ers \gt numbers of red and blue flowers and equal number of } \\ \text { red and blue flowers) } \\ \end{array} \\ \hline \text { White X Red } & \begin{array}{l} \\ \text { All flowers are red or some are red and some are white (equal } \\ \text { number of red and white flowers) } \\ \end{array} \\ \hline \text { White X Blue } & \begin{array}{l} \\ \text { All flowers are blue or some are blue and some are white (equal } \\ \text { number of blue and white flowers) } \\ \end{array} \\ \hline \text { White X Purple } & \text { Blue and red flowers (equal number of red and blue flowers) } \\ \hline \text { Red X Blue } & \begin{array}{l} \\ \text { All flowers are purple or some are red, some are blue and some } \\ \text { are white } \\ \end{array} \\ \hline \text { Red X Purple } & \text { Mostly red and purple flowers and some are blue } \\ \hline \text { Blue X Purple } & \text { Mostly blue and purple flowers and some are red } \\ \hline \\ \end{array}$
Based on this information, the correct option is:
options: There are two alleles governing flower colour.
Purple allele is dominant over Red allele, and Red allele is dominant over Blue allele.
Red allele and Blue allele show incomplete dominance.
White allele is dominant over purple allele.
